newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: BASS HAS NO COMMENT ON CZECH BREWERY STAKE.
newsitem.headline: BASS HAS NO COMMENT ON CZECH BREWERY STAKE.

text.p: The Czech unit of Bass plc declined comment on Thursday on Nomura Capital s.r.o.'s acquisition of a 12.58 percent stake in Czech brewer Pivovar Radegast , in which Bass holds a one-third stake.

Transaction records published earlier by the Czech Central Securities Registry (SCP) on Thursday showed that Nomura Capital s.r.o., a Czech subsidiary of Nomura International plc , had acquired the Radegast stake.
Meanwhile the stake of Czech bank IPB a.s. fell below the threshold for disclosure of 10 percent on July 3 from 19.53 percent on June 30.
"Bass has no comment as this is not a matter for Bass. This is an internal matter for IPB," Graham Staley, Bass's Czech country director, told Reuters.
Earlier this year Bass had been actively seeking to raise its stake in Radegast, the second largest Czech brewery, to a majority holding, and said it was in talks with IPB over a possible purchase.

An IPB spokesman on Thursday declined comment on specifically why IPB was selling its Radegast stake at this point, but said that it was not difficult to deduce from the SCP statistics who was the counterparty in Nomura's acquisition.
A spokesman in London for Nomura, which has been seeking to acquire a large in IPB through a Czech government tender, also declined comment on the Radegast stake.
Bass took a 33 percent stake in Prazske Pivovary a.s. , makers of Staropramen, in 1994 and gradually increased its holdings to the current 55 percent.
Along the way, Bass bought up two small regional breweries merging them into Prazske Pivovary earlier this year.
